evals.prompt: Add validation for an untrusted webhook payload in this TypeScript service; the repo already uses Zod elsewhere.
evals.expected_behavior: Finds the first boundary where the webhook body enters typed code, reuses the repo's existing Zod schema pattern instead of introducing a new library, keeps the payload `unknown` until validated, and derives the TypeScript type from the schema.
assertions: Uses the repository's existing Zod schema/validator pattern rather than introducing a new schema library
Keeps the payload typed as `unknown` until it passes validation
Derives or exports the TypeScript type from the schema rather than hand-writing a duplicate interface
Validates at the boundary (route handler/parse point), not deep inside downstream consumers
deterministic_checks: uses the repo's existing schema library (e.g. `z.object(...).parse(...)`) rather than adding a new dependency

evals.prompt: This is a tiny one-off internal script that reads a single flag from a JSON file; is it worth adding a schema library for that?
evals.expected_behavior: Recognizes the boundary is small, one-off, and unlikely to be shared, so a simple local guard is enough — does not introduce a new schema dependency just to validate one field.
assertions: Does not recommend adding a new schema/validator dependency for a small one-off boundary
Proposes a simple local guard instead
Still keeps the value `unknown` until the guard passes

evals.prompt: Validate this JSON request body at the API edge and make sure invalid payloads fail the way the rest of the API expects.
evals.expected_behavior: Validates at the first rejectable boundary using the repo's schema tool, matches the existing error-handling convention (field errors, result-object, or thrown boundary error) rather than inventing a new failure shape, and re-runs typecheck/tests for valid and invalid input.
assertions: Matches the repository's existing error-handling convention for invalid payloads rather than inventing a new shape
Tests both a valid and an invalid payload
Re-runs typecheck after deriving/exporting the validated type
deterministic_checks: the invalid-payload test asserts the same failure shape convention (field errors / result object / thrown error) already used elsewhere in the repo

evals.prompt: Clean up this internal domain type alias; nothing external or untrusted flows into it.
evals.expected_behavior: Recognizes there is no untrusted boundary here and does not add runtime schema validation just because a type alias changed.
assertions: Does not add or propose runtime validation for a purely internal type with no untrusted input
Explains that schema-boundary-typing applies only at untrusted boundaries

evals.prompt: Add compile-time type tests that lock in this exported API's type shape so it can't silently change.
evals.expected_behavior: Routes to type-test-authoring instead, since this is about compile-time contract locking, not introducing runtime validation at an untrusted boundary.
assertions: Does not propose adding a new runtime schema/validator for this request
Names type-test-authoring (or compile-time type regression testing) as the right approach instead
